content.title: About
content.content: Quinoa is the seed of the plant Chenopodium quinoa, native to the high‑altitude regions of the Andes. Quinoa flour is made by grinding dried seeds into a fine powder. It has a mild nutty flavor, high nutritional value, and is suitable for gluten‑free diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Quinoa is often called the “golden grain” because of its bright golden hue.
The seeds contain all nine essential amino acids, making them a complete protein source.
Quinoa was a staple food of the ancient Inca civilization.
Quinoa flour retains most of the seed’s nutrients, including fiber and micronutrients.
Quinoa is drought‑tolerant and can grow on poor soils, making it an important crop for food security.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Quinoa flour provides about 14 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport, while magnesium supports nerve and muscle function.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Naturally free of gluten, quinoa flour is safe for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Quinoa contains flavonoids and polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Saponin content
items.content: Saponins can cause mild stomach irritation; rinsing and soaking the seeds before grinding reduces them.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may be allergic to quinoa.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Quinoa flour is relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Quinoa flour can be used in baking (bread, pancakes, muffins), as a thickener for sauces, in smoothies, and for breading. It blends well with other gluten‑free flours to improve texture. Sift before use for best results.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store quinoa flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
